messages:
julie-sales: quick heads-up — acme POC is seeing repeated 429s during a bulk embeddings import. demo in ~30m, they want a walkthrough and we need to avoid a live fail. can we triage now?
omar-eng: copying logs now. are these 429s per-route or account-wide? any response headers?
julie-sales: getting the report from the customer — they say it spikes when they send ~200 parallel /embeddings calls. some succeed, others get 429s. they pasted one curl response header: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 24
x-token-budget: 0
content-type: application/json
```
kevin-oncall: thanks. that looks like a per-account token budget exhaustion. x-rate-limit-reset=24 (secs) — short window. are they using chunked batching?
sasha-ps: acme's integration spawns separate clients per user (so ~200 connections). we recommended single client + batch calls but they didn't change. can we temporarily raise their per-route burst for the demo?
dean-ops: we can do a temporary soft bump on their demo tenant for up to +3x burst for 1h, but need eng signoff. will also add audit note.
omar-eng: quick options: 1) raise per-route burst/burst-window for their tenant 2) advise them to use client-side concurrency limit to ~10 and use server-side batching 3) enable short-lived per-route reservation (if available) 4) route heavy requests to dedicated node pool (if customer has dedicated)
julie-sales: they are on a self-serve sandbox tenant (no dedicated). option 1 sounds best for demo. what's safe to change without breaking others?
kevin-oncall: safe delta: increase burst window by 2x and token bucket capacity +50% for that route. set an automated rollback in 1h. I'll apply a scoped patch to their tenant token bucket if ops approves.
dean-ops: applied request for scoped increase, pending eng approval. logged as: "temp-burst bump - acme-demo - reason: live demo"
omar-eng: if you need quick mitigation without infra change, we can also change our client-side guidance template and give acme a tiny wrapper script to limit concurrency. e.g.:
```
# bash concurrency limiter
parallel=10
xargs -P $parallel -n1 curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d @payload.json
```
sasha-ps: can you also share exact headers they should inspect so they don't confuse token budget vs rate limit? they'd appreciate clarity.
omar-eng: yes. send them this snippet to inspect:
```
# sample response headers to watch
x-rate-limit-limit: total reqs allowed in window
x-rate-limit-remaining: remaining reqs
x-rate-limit-reset: seconds until reset
x-token-budget: remaining token budget for heavy ops (embeds/generation)
```
julie-sales: dean, can we expedite the ops patch? demo in 30. if not, i'll send the wrapper script and ask acme to lower concurrency.
dean-ops: i'll mark it high priority. ops change queued, ETA ~12 minutes. rollback auto at +60m.
deploy-bot: change request 78910: "temp-burst bump - acme-demo" moved to applying -> active. audit id 78910-AUD.
omar-eng: post-patch: monitor their errors and watch for 429s. if still see 429 but headers show remaining >0, paste sample. could be per-route cap or a downstream proxy.
julie-sales: i'll coordinate with acme and report back in #sales after the demo. thanks team! :pray:
